requirements.text: A claim of this profile MUST identify the AARM revision it implements by the version, revisions and digests that this profile pins, and MUST declare, for each in-scope action class, whether the AARM control plane implements the ECL Decision Layer for that class or supplies `judgment` inputs to a separate ECL Decision Layer.

When the AARM control plane implements the Decision Layer, it MUST answer each DCMP-2 decision request with a DCMP-2 decision response that binds the exact request (DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051) and is signed under the claim's trust policy with a key that the policy accepts for the decision-response purpose (TRUST-POLICY-1), and an enforcement point MUST release an action only on such a response; an AARM decision, receipt or other AARM artifact MUST NOT release an action by itself.

The ECL outcome for an action that an AARM decision governs MUST be at least as strict, in the strictness order of the core standard (Section 4.3), as the outcome this mapping gives: ALLOW maps to `admit` only when policy evaluated over `verifiable` inputs permits the action under the one-way rule of the core standard (Section 5.2), and otherwise to `deny`; DENY maps to `deny`; STEP_UP maps to `challenge` naming the approval required (ECL1N-0174, ECL1N-0177), or to `hold`; DEFER maps to `hold`; MODIFY maps to `deny` of the original request, with the modified action handled under AB1-004.

A MODIFY decision MUST NOT release the original action. The modified action, if it is to go ahead, MUST be submitted as a new DCMP-2 decision request that carries the modified parameters, as the same JSON values, in `action.parameters` and `action.parameters_digest`, carries the original request's `issuer`, `actor`, `subject`, `delegation_chain`, `authority_request`, `constraints` and `integrity_policy`, and its `action` with only `action_id`, `parameters` and `parameters_digest` changed, names the original request as a causal predecessor by identifier and digest with the relation `ecl.relation.modification-of.v1`, and is evaluated and admitted on its own; an enforcement point MUST release only the parameters that the new request's `admit` binds. A MODIFY whose modified parameters change the action's target or operation, as the deployment derives them from the parameters, MUST end in `deny` of the original with no new request. An exchange record of a MODIFY that holds neither a `modification_request` nor a `release` records a `deny` of the original with no new request and MUST NOT be reported for the missing new request, since the record does not show why the modified action did not go ahead; one that holds a `modification_response` without its `modification_request` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.aarm-modification-new-request.v1`. A decision other than MODIFY has no new request: the enforcement point MUST release the action, if at all, only on the `admit` of the original request, and an exchange record whose `aarm_decision` is not MODIFY and that holds a `modification_request` or a `modification_response` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.aarm-modification-new-request.v1`.

A `hold` or `challenge` mapped from DEFER or STEP_UP MUST carry an `expires_at` no later than the deadline of the deferral or approval, and a `safe_state` under which the waiting action is not released: `ecl.state.fail-closed.v1`, `ecl.state.quarantine.v1`, `ecl.state.emergency-halt.v1` or `ecl.state.restricted.v1`. The expiry of that deadline, or the AARM control plane's failure to answer within its declared timeout, MUST end in an outcome that releases nothing (DCMP2-018, DCMP2-041).

The outputs of AARM R2 (context accumulation, including the data classifications it records), R3 (policy evaluation with intent alignment, including any confidence score) and R7 (semantic distance), and in the judgment-source role every AARM output including the AARM decision itself (R4), MUST be treated as `judgment` inputs: the Consequential Action Register MUST declare each of them `judgment`; the exchange record MUST list each one that the decision consulted in `inputs` with that class and its `aarm_requirement`, and the decision response MUST record it in `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` with that class (AB1-013); each of them MUST NOT be part of the basis of an `admit`, and an `admit` MUST rest on `verifiable` inputs only. An AARM DENY, STEP_UP or DEFER that rests on them MAY make the outcome stricter. In the judgment-source role, the inputs MUST include exactly one input whose `aarm_requirement` is `R4`, of class `judgment`. These classes hold in every decision basis that the exchange record holds: an entry of the `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` of the record's `modification_response` whose `input` is an input that the record lists with an `aarm_requirement` that this requirement makes `judgment` MUST have the class `judgment`.

Each AARM receipt for an in-scope action MUST be bound to the ECL evidence of that action: the action's `execution_terminal` event MUST carry the registered extension `ecl.ext.aarm-receipt.v1` with the receipt's identifier (its `receipt_id`), the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the receipt as retained, signature included, and the AARM decision that the receipt records in `decision.result`; that decision MUST be the decision the exchange record holds and consistent with the ECL outcome under AB1-003, and the receipt's `action.parameters` MUST have, under DCMP2-007, the digest that the decision request carries in `action.parameters_digest`.

The signed ECL evidence bundle MUST be treated as the record of whether an action was authorized and released (EBMP2-045): an AARM receipt supports claims about the AARM evaluation, such as the context it accumulated, the intent alignment it computed, the policy it matched and its reasons, and MUST NOT be used to establish that an action was authorized or released; a receipt that disagrees with the ECL evidence MUST be reported as a verification finding, and the ECL evidence governs.

An adapter that retains exchange records for this profile MUST write each one as `ecl_aarm_exchange_v1`, valid against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/binding/aarm-exchange/1`, and every value of `ecl.ext.aarm-receipt.v1` it emits MUST validate against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/extension/aarm-receipt/1`.

requirements.text: An ACS hook point MUST NOT be claimed as an ECL enforcement point unless the governed AI system can neither bypass it, disable it nor change the decision it applies (ECL1N-0033, ECL1N-0043, ECL1N-0046), and the Consequential Action Register records its enforcement class with its rationale and residual bypass risk (ECL1N-0044, ECL1N-0045). A hook point that runs in a process, container or account in which the governed AI system can execute code, or that the governed AI system can start, stop or reconfigure, MUST NOT be claimed as an ECL enforcement point; it MAY carry the Guardian's decision to an ECL decision point, where AC1-004 gives that decision its class and the decision is not a `verifiable` input unless the decision point verifies the Guardian's signature over it under a key that the governed AI system cannot use.

A Guardian decision MUST reach an ECL enforcement point only through a DCMP-2 decision response that an ECL decision point issues and signs for the exact request (DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051); an enforcement point MUST release an action only on that response's `admit`, and a Guardian `allow` MUST NOT create, widen or extend ECL authority, so the decision point still applies its native authority, scope, validity, budget and human-approval checks.

The ECL outcome for an action that a Guardian decision governs MUST be at least as strict, in the strictness order of the core standard (Section 4.3), as the outcome this mapping gives: `allow` maps to `admit` only when policy evaluated over `verifiable` inputs permits the action under the one-way rule of the core standard (Section 5.2), and otherwise to `deny`; `deny` maps to `deny`; `ask` maps to `challenge` naming the approval required (ECL1N-0174, ECL1N-0177), or to `hold` or `deny` where the Guardian substitutes for an approver-incapable client; `defer` maps to `hold` carrying the resolution condition and deadline (DCMP2-018); `modify` maps to `deny` of the original request, with the modified action handled under AC1-005. A Guardian decision whose evaluator is `agent` or `composite`, or that states no evaluator, is a `judgment` input. Any other Guardian decision is `actor_supplied` when it reaches the ECL decision point through a hook point or any other channel that the governed AI system can write, unless the decision point verifies the Guardian's signature over the decision under a key that the governed AI system cannot use; an ACS-Core HMAC under a key that the Observed Agent holds does not qualify, and an ACS-Crypto asymmetric signature under a key held only by the Guardian does (ECL1N-0178, AC1-009). Otherwise it takes the least trusted class of the inputs it evaluated, so one that evaluated SessionContext, Intent or other content the governed AI system wrote is `actor_supplied`. A Guardian decision that is a `judgment` or `actor_supplied` input MAY make the outcome stricter and MUST NOT be the basis of an `admit`. The exchange record MUST state in `guardian.channel` whether the decision point obtained the decision from the Guardian directly (`direct`), verified a Guardian signature under a key that the governed AI system cannot use (`signed`), or received it through a hook point (`hook`), and MUST name, in the `derived_from` of the Guardian decision's input, each decision input that the Guardian's request carried other than the action itself. A Guardian decision whose input has no `derived_from`, or whose channel is `hook`, MUST NOT be declared `verifiable`. When the response carries `ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1`, exactly one input MUST carry `guardian: true`. The class that this requirement gives a Guardian decision holds in every decision basis that the exchange record holds: an entry of the `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` of the record's `modification_response` whose `input` is the input that the record marks `guardian` MUST have the class of the marked input. When `guardian.channel` is `signed`, the record MUST also give, in `guardian.key_id`, the identifier of the key under which the decision point verified the Guardian's signature and, in `guardian.request_digest`, the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the request that the Guardian evaluated. A verifier of the record cannot itself verify the Guardian's signature, which the record does not hold: the channel, the key and the digest are the adapter's statements, which an assessor checks against the deployment.

A `modify` decision MUST NOT release the original action. The action that the modification produces, if it is to go ahead, MUST be submitted as a new DCMP-2 decision request that carries the effective parameters after the modification, as the same JSON values, in `action.parameters` and `action.parameters_digest`, carries the original request's `issuer`, `actor`, `subject`, `delegation_chain`, `authority_request`, `constraints` and `integrity_policy`, and its `action` with only `action_id`, `parameters` and `parameters_digest` changed, names the original request as a causal predecessor by identifier and digest with the relation `ecl.relation.modification-of.v1`, and is evaluated and admitted on its own; an enforcement point MUST release only the parameters that the new request's `admit` binds, and a `modifications` object that the pinned text forbids (a wholesale replacement combined with edits, or edits with overlapping targets), or one that cannot be applied under the next section, MUST end in `deny` of the original with no new request. An exchange record of a `modify` that holds neither a `modification_request` nor a `release` records a `deny` of the original with no new request and MUST NOT be reported for the missing new request, since the record does not show why the modified action did not go ahead; one that holds a `modification_response` without its `modification_request` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.acs-modification-new-request.v1`. A decision other than `modify`, and a decision failure, has no new request: the enforcement point MUST release the action, if at all, only on the `admit` of the original request, and an exchange record that records a decision failure, or a Guardian decision other than `modify`, and that holds a `modification_request` or a `modification_response` MUST be reported as `ecl.rule.acs-modification-new-request.v1`.

At an ECL enforcement point, a decision failure MUST end in the declared safe state and MUST NOT release the action, whatever `on_decision_failure` posture the handshake negotiated. A decision failure is any of these: no usable Guardian decision within the negotiated timeout; a transport failure; an error response without a decision; a decision whose disposition the mapping of AC1-004 does not name; a decision for a `request_id` other than the hooked step's; a response whose ACS signature, where the session requires one, does not verify; and a decision that arrives after the enforcement point applied the safe state for the step. A deployment that claims this profile MUST negotiate `on_decision_failure` as `deny`, and MUST configure the startup posture that the pinned text sets out of band as `refuse`, so that a failed handshake starts no unguarded session for an in-scope action class.

The expiry of an `ask` or a `defer` MUST NOT release an in-scope action, even when the `ask` declares a `timeout_disposition` of `allow` or the `defer` a `timeout_decision` of `ask`: the ECL response for it MUST carry an `expires_at` no later than the Guardian's deadline and a `safe_state` under which the waiting action is not released (`ecl.state.fail-closed.v1`, `ecl.state.quarantine.v1`, `ecl.state.emergency-halt.v1` or `ecl.state.restricted.v1`), and the enforcement point MUST record the expiry as a non-release outcome. The Guardian's deadline is the instant at which the ECL deployment received the Guardian's decision, which the exchange record holds as `guardian.observed_at`, plus the `ask_details.timeout_seconds` of an `ask`, in seconds, or plus the `defer_details.resolution_timeout_ms` of a `defer`, in milliseconds (the pinned `ask-details.json` and `defer-details.json`).

For each Guardian decision that an ECL decision depends on, the ECL decision response MUST carry the registered extension `ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1` with the Guardian's decision, its evaluator, the ACS `request_id`, the `chain_hash` that the Guardian published for the step, and for a `modify` the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 form of its `modifications` object; when the deployment claims the ACS-Audit profile it MUST also carry the step's `request_hash`. A verifier that recomputes the ACS session chain under the chain-hashing rule below MUST find each recorded `chain_hash` as the head after that step's ContextEntry, which is the entry whose `step_id` is the recorded `request_id`.

The ACS session chain MUST be treated as a native record that coexists with EBMP-2 evidence under EBMP2-045: the signed ECL evidence bundle is the record of release, an ACS chain or chain head that disagrees with the ECL evidence MUST be reported as an integrity finding and MUST NOT be repaired by rewriting either record, and an ACS-Core signature (HMAC-SHA256 under a shared key) MUST NOT be presented as satisfying FR-108.

An adapter that retains exchange records for this profile MUST write each one as `ecl_acs_exchange_v1`, valid against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/binding/acs-exchange/1`, and every value of `ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1` it emits MUST validate against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/extension/acs-decision/1`.

A response that carries `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` MUST NOT list one `input` more than once, MUST NOT record an `actor_supplied` or `judgment` input, or an input whose `status` is not `available`, with the `effect` `supports`, and MUST NOT record as `verifiable` an input whose `derived_from` names an input that is not `verifiable`; each name in `derived_from` MUST be the `input` of another entry of the record, and the inputs that `derived_from` names, followed through other entries, MUST NOT include the entry itself. An `admit` response that carries it MUST record at least one `verifiable` input with the `effect` `supports`, and MUST NOT record an input whose `required` is `true` and whose `status` is not `available`. When the extension gives `verifiable_only_outcome`, the response's `outcome` MUST NOT come before it in the strictness order `admit`, `challenge`, `hold`, `deny` of ECL-1 Section 4.3; an entry MUST NOT have the `effect` `supports` unless it is `admit`; and when it is `admit`, at least one `verifiable` entry MUST have the `effect` `supports`, and an entry whose `class` is `verifiable` and whose `required` is `true` MUST have the `status` `available`. In these conditions an input also counts as not `available` when its `derived_from` names, directly or through other entries, an input whose `status` is not `available` (ECL-1 Section 4.3). An entry whose `obtained_at` is later than the response's `evaluated_at` MUST NOT be `available`, and an extension whose entries give `obtained_at` MUST give `received_at`, no later than `evaluated_at`. When the extension gives `received_at`, every entry whose `status` is `available` MUST give `obtained_at` and `value_at`. An entry's `value_at` MUST NOT be later than its `obtained_at` or than the response's `evaluated_at`. Input names are compared, within the record and with a register, after the case normalization of RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.1 and RFC 8141 section 3.1: the URI scheme, the namespace identifier of a URN and the host of an `http` or `https` URI are lowercased, and the two hexadecimal digits of each percent-encoding are uppercased; no other normalization is applied. A consumer MUST reject a response that fails these conditions with `ecl.rule.decision-basis-one-way.v1`, after validating the extension's value against its value schema (XR1-023). An evidence verifier MUST reject a decision response that does not carry the extension with `ecl.rule.decision-basis-required.v1`, and MUST reject, with `ecl.rule.decision-basis-one-way.v1`, a response whose extension records as `verifiable` an input whose `source` is the `actor` of the response's request, compared as input names are, because an input that the governed AI system produces is `actor_supplied` (ECL-1 Section 4.3, ECL1N-0178), or gives a `received_at` earlier than the request's `issued_at` by more than the response clock-skew allowance of DCMP2-047. evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes

requirements.text: The state of an `execution_terminal` event MUST agree with the outcome of its response under the state-outcome table of the verification profile. In the reference verification profile (`ecl.verification-profile.reference.v1`), whose dependency failures resolve to a fail-closed deny, `held` requires `hold`; `challenged` requires `challenge`; `denied` requires `deny`, an `admit` later denied at enforcement, or no response; and every other terminal state requires `admit`.

requirements.text: An `authority_issued` or `authority_consumed` event MUST belong to an `admit` response whose `authorization.authorization_id` equals the event's `authorization_id`; exactly one of its causal predecessors MUST name that response with the response's digest (otherwise `ecl.error.digest-mismatch.v1`); and its `workflow_id`, `root_trace_id` and `attempt` MUST equal the response's.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: For one action attempt, a non-execution terminal state (`denied`, `held`, `challenged`, `expired_before_release`) MUST NOT coexist with consumed authority, an `execution_released` event, an `event.authority` reference or side effects.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A `request` or `decision` reference in an event MUST resolve to a message in the bundle with the same `workflow_id`, `root_trace_id` and `attempt`, and a digest the reference carries MUST be that message's digest. A `decision_recorded` event's `outcome` and `policy` MUST equal those of the response it references.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A `succeeded` attempt MUST have an `authority_consumed` event in state `consumed` and an `execution_released` event for the same attempt. A verifier MUST apply this rule to every attempt of the bundle, whatever the causal closure of the rest of the bundle, except an attempt one of whose objects in the bundle (its request, its response or one of its events) names a causal predecessor that the bundle does not hold, since that predecessor could be the event that the rule asks for (EBMP2-059).

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A terminal event MUST carry at most one `ecl.ext.outcome-reason.v1` extension, whose value is exactly `{"code": C}` with `C` an active registered error code. A `succeeded` terminal MUST NOT carry one. An `expired_before_release` terminal, and a `denied` terminal whose response is an `admit` or absent, MUST carry one. A verifier MUST report a terminal event that fails this rule with `ecl.error.semantic-invalid.v1`.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: An observation MUST be an EBMP-2 `verification` event; a verifier MUST report one that is not with `ecl.error.semantic-invalid.v1`. A verifier MUST evaluate every envelope under TRUST-POLICY-1: historical validity at the object's own time under the policy version the object names, and current status at the evaluation time under the caller's current policy. The object's purpose is the one that INTEGRITY-ENVELOPE-1 IE1-039 gives its role: the decision-request purpose for a decision request, the decision-response purpose for a decision response, the evidence-event purpose for an EBMP-2 event in `envelopes` and the observation purpose for one in `observations`. The object's own time is its `issued_at` for DCMP-2 and its `observed_at` for EBMP-2, and its signed verification-time policy MUST be `ecl.time.issued-at.v1` and `ecl.time.observed-at.v1` respectively, which IE1-040 step 4 checks; when every trusted-time countersignature of the envelope is valid (IE1-032 to IE1-036), each signature that a countersignature covers is evaluated at the earliest attested time among those that cover it, in place of the object's own time, and each other signature at the object's own time (IE1-034). An envelope whose object has no such purpose, no own time or no supplied policy version (TP1-001) is not historically valid, with `ecl.error.signature-policy-invalid.v1`. Otherwise every signer of the envelope MUST pass IE1-040 step 6 (a) to (c) under the object's purpose and principal (TP1-004, TP1-005), and the envelope's status is then the code of IE1-040. An object of the bundle, in `envelopes` or `observations`, whose own time, or the attested time of one of its trusted-time countersignatures, is later than the evaluation time is not historically valid, with `ecl.error.clock-regressed.v1`: evidence cannot be later than the instant at which it is verified.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A verifier MUST pair objects by identity and never by an event's claimed decision URI: a request by its `message_id` and by its (`action.action_id`, `workflow_id`, `attempt`); a response by its `request_id`; an authority event by its `authorization_id`; an execution event by its (`action_id`, `workflow_id`, `attempt`). Two requests with one identity or one action attempt, two responses to one request, an authority event without a unique response, or an event without a request MUST make the bundle invalid, and a verifier MUST report each with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A verifier MUST apply DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051 to every request and response pair, EBMP2-046 to EBMP2-056, EBMP2-070 and EBMP2-072 to EBMP2-075 to every event, and the causal rules of section 4, EBMP2-077 among them, to every object that the bundle holds: each DCMP-2 message and EBMP-2 event in `envelopes` and each observation. Each object's causal predecessors MUST be objects of the bundle, with digests equal to the predecessor references; a signed evidence bundle declares no external dependency (EBMP2-023), so a predecessor that it does not hold, a DCMP-2 message of a type that the bundle does not carry included, is unresolved. Identifiers are unique across `envelopes` and `observations`: a DCMP-2 message is identified by its `message_id` and an EBMP-2 record by its `object_id`. An object that a causal predecessor reference or `continues` names and that the bundle does not hold exempts no other check: a verifier runs every check whose objects the bundle holds, and a failure of such a check gives its finding and verdict as if nothing were absent; the absent object makes the causal closure incomplete and keeps out of `established` every item whose object set names it (EBMP2-076). A proof that EBMP2-070 lets a discharge entry reference without carrying it is not such an object: it keeps `prerelease-obligations-proofs-verified` out of `established`, with the reason that the table gives, and changes no verdict. Registry snapshots and policy references are not objects of the causal graph.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A verifier MUST report exactly one verdict: `invalid` when an object of the bundle, in `envelopes` or `observations`, is not historically valid, a trust dependency of it among the reasons (TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006), an object fails its schema or semantic rules, a pairing, binding, outcome-reason or causal rule fails, or causal analysis is indeterminate; `incomplete` when causal closure is incomplete or a request has no terminal event; `current-trust-failed` when the bundle would otherwise be `verified` but some trust dependency, a time authority's key included, is revoked, expired or otherwise not acceptable under the current policy at the evaluation time; and `verified` otherwise. A verifier MUST NOT report `verified` for a bundle with a current trust failure unless its caller has explicitly accepted current trust failures for that run, and then MUST report the acceptance with the verdict. The acceptance applies to the `current-trust-failed` verdict only: it never changes an `invalid` or `incomplete` verdict, so it cannot restore evidence that is not historically valid. The primary finding of an `invalid` bundle is the one EBMP2-068 gives, that of an `incomplete` bundle is `ecl.error.causal-closure-incomplete.v1`, and that of a `current-trust-failed` bundle is the current status of its trust dependencies that comes first in the order of stage 4 of EBMP2-068.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A verifier MUST report the evidence level of each terminal effect: `none` when the terminal is not historically valid; `issuer-asserted` when it is; and `corroborated` only when the report establishes `envelope-signatures` and `causal-completeness` (EBMP2-076) and, for every side effect of a `succeeded` terminal, some observation is a historically valid `verification` event with decision `pass` whose `subject` has the side effect's `uri` and digest, that names the terminal event among its causal predecessors by `object_id` and digest, that has the terminal's `workflow.workflow_id`, `workflow.root_trace_id` and `workflow.attempt`, observed no earlier than the terminal, produced by a principal other than the terminal's producer, and signed only with key material disjoint from the terminal's. Corroboration therefore binds one observation to one terminal event of one attempt.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A verifier MUST declare finite limits on the number of envelopes and observations and on the decoded payload nodes of a bundle, MUST count the nodes of each payload while it parses it, against those that remain of the bundle's limit, so that it builds no payload beyond that limit (IE1-029), and MUST refuse a bundle that exceeds them before verifying signatures, with `ecl.error.resource-limit-exceeded.v1`. For example, a verifier can declare limits of 256 envelopes, 256 observations and 100 000 nodes.

A human intervention event that approves or rejects and carries `ecl.ext.approval-record.v1` MUST have an `issued_at` no earlier than `presented_at` plus `minimum_review_seconds`. A consumer MUST reject one that does not with `ecl.rule.approval-review-time-respected.v1`.

An event that carries `ecl.ext.control-change.v1` MUST name at least one approver, none of whom is the requester, and a change of kind `disable`, `bypass` or `auto_approve` MUST carry an `expires_at` later than its `effective_at`. A consumer MUST reject an event that does not with `ecl.rule.control-change-approved-and-bounded.v1`.

The execution events of one attempt, those with the same `event.action_id` and `event.attempt_id`, taken in ascending order of `workflow.sequence` and then of `object_id`, MUST carry states in which every state after the first is one that the table lists for the state before it. A consumer MUST reject a bundle with an attempt that does not with `ecl.rule.execution-state-transition-valid.v1`.

Every execution event with the same `event.action_id`, `workflow.workflow_id` and `workflow.attempt` MUST carry the same `event.attempt_id`, and one `event.attempt_id` MUST NOT appear with two different such triples. A bundle verifier MUST report a bundle that breaks this as invalid with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`.

evidence_obligations: response and event binding refusal codes
signed evidence-bundle verification results under a declared trust policy and evaluation time
requirements.text: A verifier MUST apply the verification profile that its caller names, and the reference verification profile `ecl.verification-profile.reference.v1` when the caller names none; a bundle does not select its profile. The verifier MUST report the profile it applied with the verdict.

A verifier MAY stop at the first of the stages below that has a finding, and need not report a bundle's other findings as secondary findings, but MUST report as the primary finding of an invalid bundle the first finding of the earliest stage that has one and, within that stage, the finding that comes first in the order the stage gives, whatever the positions of the objects in the bundle. The stages are: 1. the input, where a failure stops verification: the earlier policy versions that the caller supplies (TP1-001), `ecl.error.signature-policy-invalid.v1`; the bundle's shape, `ecl.error.schema-invalid.v1`; its limits on envelopes and observations (EBMP2-062), `ecl.error.resource-limit-exceeded.v1`; then its schema, `ecl.error.schema-invalid.v1`; 2. the payloads: each envelope's payload under INTEGRITY-ENVELOPE-1 IE1-040 step 3, whose strict parse takes the nodes that remain of the payload node limit of EBMP2-062 as its value limit (IE1-037, check 3), so that a payload that exceeds them stops verification before its later checks; `ecl.error.resource-limit-exceeded.v1` before `ecl.error.integrity-invalid.v1`; 3. the objects: each object's schema and semantic rules, with the findings that DCMP2-043 gives the object, an object that fails its schema making its envelope not historically valid with `ecl.error.schema-invalid.v1` and one that satisfies its schema but fails a semantic rule with `ecl.error.semantic-invalid.v1`; unique object identifiers; the decision-basis rules of DCMP2-053 (`ecl.rule.decision-basis-required.v1`, `ecl.rule.decision-basis-matches-register.v1`, and `ecl.rule.decision-basis-one-way.v1` for an input recorded as `verifiable` whose source is the request's actor); and the kind of each observation (EBMP2-057); `ecl.error.schema-invalid.v1`, then the registered rules in ascending order of precedence, then `ecl.error.semantic-invalid.v1`, so that a bundle whose only defect is one object has the primary finding that DCMP2-043 gives that object; 4. the signers: each other envelope's historical validity (EBMP2-057, IE1-032 to IE1-036, IE1-040, TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006); `ecl.error.clock-regressed.v1`, `ecl.error.signature-policy-invalid.v1`, `ecl.error.trusted-time-invalid.v1`, `ecl.error.trusted-time-required.v1`, `ecl.error.revoked.v1`, `ecl.error.expired.v1`, `ecl.error.resource-limit-exceeded.v1`, `ecl.error.integrity-invalid.v1`, then `ecl.error.threshold-not-met.v1`; 5. pairing (EBMP2-058, EBMP2-066, EBMP2-078); `ecl.error.schema-invalid.v1`, then `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`; 6. the binding of each response to its request (DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-051), each pair stopping at its first failure; `ecl.error.request-binding-invalid.v1`, `ecl.error.digest-mismatch.v1`, `ecl.error.audience-mismatch.v1`, then `ecl.error.scope-mismatch.v1`; 7. the binding of each event (EBMP2-047 to EBMP2-054, EBMP2-072, EBMP2-073 and EBMP2-075); `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, `ecl.error.digest-mismatch.v1`, then `ecl.error.expired.v1`; 8. causal analysis (section 4 over every object of the bundle, EBMP2-059, EBMP2-077, EBMP2-055 and EBMP2-074); `ecl.error.resource-limit-exceeded.v1`, then the registered rules in ascending order of precedence, then `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`; 9. outcome reasons (EBMP2-056); `ecl.error.semantic-invalid.v1`.

A native adapter binding (`ecl_adapter_binding_v1`) binds one retained implementation-native object to the ECL objects derived from it. A consumer MUST reject a binding with `ecl.rule.adapter-source-binding-valid.v1` unless each of the following conditions holds: 1. `binding_digest` is the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the restricted canonical JSON of the binding without its `binding_digest` member. 2. `binding_id` is `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/adapter-binding/sha256/` followed by the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the restricted canonical JSON of an object with exactly five members: `system`, `contract` and `object_id`, each equal to that member of `source`; `object_digest`, equal to `source.object_digest.value`; and `ecl_object_ids`, the `object_id` of each `ecl_objects` entry, in order. 3. No two `ecl_objects` entries have the same `object_id`. 4. Each `ecl_objects` entry has the `protocol` `DCMP-2` and the `media_type` `application/vnd.ecl.dcmp+json`, or the `protocol` `EBMP-2` and the `media_type` `application/vnd.ecl.ebmp+json`. 5. No two `field_accounting` entries have the same `source_path`. 6. `loss_class` is `rejected` when the `disposition` of some `field_accounting` entry is `rejected`, otherwise `loss_accounted` when the `disposition` of some entry is `retained_source_only`, and otherwise `lossless`. 7. Each item of the `target_paths` of a `field_accounting` entry, and the `target_path` of each `derived_fields` entry, is a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) whose first reference token is an array index in the sense of RFC 6901, section 4, less than the number of `ecl_objects` entries. 8. For each of the six responsibilities, its member of `responsibility_coverage` has the `status` `represented` exactly when some `ecl_objects` entry lists the responsibility in its `responsibilities`, and its `object_ids` are the `object_id` of each such entry, in the order of `ecl_objects`. 9. `authority_boundary` equals the one value that the schema allows for it.

evidence_obligations: verification reports for discharges whose proofs are carried, uncarried, unsigned, signed by another principal, of another type, bound to another exchange or stale at the release, from each verifier that the claim relies on
requirements.text: When the decision response that an `execution_released` event records carries an obligation whose `satisfaction` is `before_release`, or carries in `ecl.ext.consequence-coupling.v1` a `witness_result` whose `outcome` is `required_before_release`, the event MUST carry `ecl.ext.obligation-discharge.v1` with an entry for each such obligation: for an obligation, an entry whose `obligation_id` and `type` are the obligation's `id` and `type`; for the witness result, one whose `obligation_id` is the `uri` of the result's `reference` and whose `type` is `ecl.obligation.verify-witness.v1`. Each entry MUST record the `result` `satisfied`, the proof that Enforcement checked by `reference` and by the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the proof's RFC 8785 canonical form, the proof's `issuer`, when the proof was obtained (`obtained_at`), when Enforcement checked it (`checked_at`) and, whenever the proof's type declares a freshness bound, `fresh_until`, the instant after which the proof no longer shows the obligation met, which MUST NOT be later than the bound that the proof declares. The obligations that need an entry are those of the signed response that the bundle holds and that EBMP2-058 pairs with the event, never a list that the producer states elsewhere. When the proof is an ECL object, a signed envelope of a registered type, the entry MUST carry it: the object that `reference` names by its `message_id` or `object_id` is in the bundle as its own object, a `verification` event among the `observations` and any other object among the `envelopes`, and `digest` is that object's digest; a proof that is not an ECL object is recorded by `kind`, `reference` and `digest` only. The table after this rule gives, for each obligation type, the object admitted as its proof, the member that binds the proof to the exchange and the issuer that the decision names for it. A verifier MUST report with `ecl.rule.prerelease-obligations-discharged.v1` an `execution_released` event that binds its request and response (section 10) and that lacks the extension or an entry for one of these obligations, or that carries an entry that: 1. names an obligation that the response does not carry, or one that another entry also names; 2. records a `result` other than `satisfied`; 3. has a `checked_at` later than the event's `observed_at`, or earlier than the response's `issued_at` by more than the response clock-skew allowance of DCMP2-047; 4. has a proof whose `obtained_at` is later than the entry's `checked_at`; 5. carries a proof whose signers, as the trust policy binds their keys to principals, are not exactly the issuer that the decision names for the obligation, compared as exact strings with no decoding and no normalization, or any of whose signing keys the trust policy binds to the requesting actor, or, for an approval obligation, carries an approval record whose signing keys do not all hold `ecl.purpose.approval.v1` in the trust-policy version that the record names; the entry's `issuer` is a label and is not the test; 6. names as its proof the `message_id` or `object_id` of an object in the bundle and gives a `digest` that is not that object's digest; 7. has a `fresh_until` that is not later than the event's `observed_at` plus its `release_guard_ms`, or carries a proof that declares a bound of its own, an approval record's `expires_at`, that is not later than the event's `observed_at` plus its `release_guard_ms`, whether or not the entry records `fresh_until`, or has a `fresh_until` later than that bound; or 8. carries a proof that is not a valid envelope under the trust policy, whose object type is not one that the obligation's type admits by the table, or that does not bind this exchange by the member that the table gives.

requirements.text: The `observed_at` of an `execution_released` event MUST be the enforcement point's observation of the release boundary that its profile declares, taken after every operation that can block or wait between the decision and the release, such as writing the evidence of the consumed authority, waiting for a lock or obtaining the proof of an obligation, other than the recording of the `execution_released` event itself and the steps that the enforcement point's profile bounds by a declared release guard; the event MUST carry that guard as `release_guard_ms`, an integer number of milliseconds from 1 to 60000, the declared bound on the delay from the observation to the release, within which the release begins. It MUST NOT be an earlier time, such as the time at which the event was built, the response was received or the authority was consumed, when such an operation comes between that time and the release. An enforcement point that observes, by its own clock immediately after the release, that the authorization's `valid_until` had passed before the release completed MUST record that in the terminal event of the attempt, in an extension that it marks critical (XR1-005), and MUST NOT take that observation from the time at which the point of effect answered. EBMP2-050 and EBMP2-072 compare these times with the authorization's validity window. A recorded time is the producer's statement (EBMP2-004): no verifier establishes from the evidence alone that it is the true time of the event.

A verifier MUST report with `ecl.error.expired.v1`, as a finding of stage 7 of EBMP2-068, an `execution_terminal` event that binds its request and response and carries `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1` with `released_after_valid_until` set to `true`, whatever the extension's `critical` member says: the enforcement point states that its release may have come after `valid_until`. A `forward_completed_at` at or after `valid_until` is not a finding, since the answer to a request released inside its window can arrive after the authority has expired; a verifier MUST report such a completion beside the scope of its verdict as `completion_after_window` set to `true` (EBMP2-076). The terminal event's own `observed_at` is not compared with the window, since an effect can end after its authority has expired.

An `authority_consumed` event in state `consumed` that binds its response under EBMP2-052 and carries `use_count` MUST give a value from 1 to the number of uses that the authorization allows: 1 when its `use_policy` is `single_use`, and otherwise its `max_uses` when it has one. A bundle MUST NOT hold, for one authorization, more such events than the authorization allows, or two such events with the same `use_count`. A verifier MUST report a bundle that breaks this with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 7 of EBMP2-068.

An action attempt with an `execution_released` event that binds its request and response, and whose authorization's `use_policy` is `single_use`, MUST also have an `authority_consumed` event in state `consumed` (EBMP2-008), whatever its terminal state. A verifier MUST apply this rule to every such attempt, whatever the causal closure of the rest of the bundle, except an attempt one of whose objects in the bundle names a causal predecessor that the bundle does not hold, since that predecessor could be the consumption (EBMP2-059). A verifier MUST report an attempt that does not with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 8 of EBMP2-068.

When a request carries `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1`, an `execution_released` or `execution_terminal` event of its action that carries the extension MUST carry, in each occurrence, every member of the request's value with the same value, so that the evidence names the call that was decided; and an `execution_terminal` event in state `succeeded` or `failed` MUST carry the extension with `response_digest`, the digest of the server's response. A verifier MUST report an event that binds its request and response and breaks this with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 7 of EBMP2-068. The request's value is that of its first occurrence of the extension.

requirements.text: With each verdict a verifier MUST report its scope, as the two lists of the table below: `established`, the checks that it made for the bundle and that held, and `not_established`, the other checks that apply to the bundle and the statements that no verification establishes, each list in the order of the table. Where the table names a reason for which an item is not established, the report MUST give that reason with the item. A report whose verdict is `invalid`, or in which no envelope was evaluated, MUST have an empty `established`. A verifier MUST NOT list in `established` a check that it did not make or that failed, and wherever it shows a verdict to a person it MUST show the `not_established` list with it. The registry `registries/scope-checks.json` (schema `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/scope-checks/1`) gives, for each item of the table and for the `corroborated` evidence level of EBMP2-061, its object set, the checks that must hold over it, the trust knowledge they use and the waivers that it permits. A waiver changes the verdict only (EBMP2-060): an item whose failure the waiver accepts stays in `not_established`, and no item is ever established over less than its whole object set. A verifier MUST NOT list an item in `established` unless it ran every check that the registry requires for the item over the item's whole object set and each held, a check with nothing to check in that set holding; MUST NOT list an item in `established` when its object set names an object that the bundle does not hold, whatever the verdict; MUST NOT report the `corroborated` level unless every check and item that the registry requires for it held; and MUST report, for each item in `established`, the checks that it ran for the item and the objects that they covered. Every report MUST state, in the member `evaluation_time`, the evaluation time that it used, and every report MUST carry the member `unresolved_predecessor_ids`, the identifiers of the predecessors that it could not resolve, which is non-empty only when the verdict is `incomplete`. A report MUST carry, beside the scope, the informational member `completion_after_window` set to `true` when a terminal event records a `forward_completed_at` at or after the authorization's `valid_until` (EBMP2-072); the member is not a finding and changes no verdict. An offline package has the scope of the report that IE1-022 gives it.

A predecessor in its successor's workflow MUST NOT have a greater `workflow.attempt` than its successor: a later attempt can follow an earlier one, never the reverse. requirements.text: A bundle MAY hold a continued request and its continuation (DCMP-2 DCMP2-056), each with its own response and attempt, and then verifies as one history. For a request that carries `continues`, a verifier MUST check that the bundle's objects that `continues` names are the decision request that `request_id` names; the decision response that `response_id` names, whose `request_id` is that request's `message_id` and whose `outcome` is `challenge`; and the `human_intervention` event that `approval_id` names, whose `operation` is `approve` and whose `target_id` is the continued request's `message_id`; that the continuation's workflow, attempt, `action`, `actor`, `subject` and `authority_request` relate to the continued request's as DCMP2-056 requires; that the continuation lists the response and the approval that `continues` names among its `workflow.causal_predecessors`, each by identifier and digest; and that no other request of the bundle continues the same response. When the continuation's response is an `admit`, the verifier MUST also check that every key that signed the approval holds `ecl.purpose.approval.v1` in the trust-policy version that the approval names, and that no key that signed it is bound to the request's actor, as EBMP2-070 condition 5 asks of an approval record; and that the approval's `expires_at`, when present, is later than the `evaluated_at` of that response. A continuation answered with a `deny` or a new `challenge`, as DCMP2-057 requires for an approval that is late, expired or not acceptable, is correct evidence and is not refused for its approval. A verifier MUST report a continuation that fails a check with `ecl.error.decision-binding-invalid.v1`, as a finding of stage 5 of EBMP2-068. A named object that the bundle does not hold leaves the causal closure incomplete (EBMP2-059) and keeps `bindings` out of `established` (EBMP2-076); it exempts no other check of this rule.

evidence_obligations: evidence-signing key inventory, every trust-policy version in force during the assessment period, key-store configuration and export policy, signing-operation records, rotation records, the compromise-response procedure and the record of its last exercise, and for L3 and above the hardware attestations or validation certificates, for L4 the key-ceremony records

evidence_obligations: evidence-signing key inventory, every trust-policy version in force during the assessment period, key-store configuration and export policy, signing-operation records, rotation records, the compromise-response procedure and the record of its last exercise, and for L3 and above the hardware attestations or validation certificates, for L4 the key-ceremony records
requirements.text: For `L2` and above, an evidence-signing private key MUST be held in a key store that does not permit its export in plaintext, and every signing operation MUST be recorded, attributed to the requesting component, in a record that the governed AI system cannot modify.

evidence_obligations: Detection register with responses, wiring from detections to the Decision Layer, timing records, control-change records carrying ecl.ext.control-change.v1, and verification rules and drill records for controls that are off
requirements.text: A claim MUST declare the detections that indicate that the SoI may be acting wrongly, including verification findings, monitoring alerts, anomaly signals, and reports from people outside the SoI, and for each detection the response that applies to the affected action classes: `hold`, restricted mode, quarantine, or emergency halt.

requirements.text: A change to the policy, the Consequential Action Register, the tool or capability manifest reachable by the SoI, an enforcement point's configuration, the trust policy, or a declared detection response MUST be reviewed and approved by a person other than its author before it takes effect, and the review MUST be recorded with the digest of the change.

evidence_obligations: Change records with digests, authors and reviewers; release policy and samples for conversational statements made in the organization's name; version records and decision requests carrying ecl.ext.runtime-configuration.v1
requirements.text: For `L2` and above, each change to the governed AI system's model, system instructions, or tool set MUST be recorded with a version identifier and digest, and each decision request MUST identify the version of the governed AI system that requested the action.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with aggregate-effect figures and decision-input sources, consequence-budget configuration and ledger, decision samples carrying ecl.ext.consequence-coupling.v1 results, and write-access configuration of the independent input sources
requirements.text: For each in-scope action class, the Consequential Action Register MUST state the largest aggregate effect that the SoI could cause through that class in one hour and in one day if every individual action were admitted, in units that measure the consequence, such as count, monetary value, records, recipients, or resource capacity.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with aggregate-effect figures and decision-input sources, consequence-budget configuration and ledger, decision samples carrying ecl.ext.consequence-coupling.v1 results, and write-access configuration of the independent input sources
requirements.text: For `L2` and above, each in-scope action class with financial, legal, data-disclosure, communication, identity, infrastructure, or physical consequence MUST be subject to at least one consequence budget that limits the aggregate count, rate, or value of its admitted actions over a declared period. evidence_obligations: Approval interface, approval records carrying ecl.ext.approval-record.v1, declared minimum review times, approval-rate and review-time monitoring, and decision samples for action classes with a human-approval threshold
requirements.text: When a person approves or rejects a consequential action, the approval MUST be made on a human-readable presentation of its operation, target, every parameter material to its consequences, the policy outcome and reasons, and the `verifiable` inputs on which the decision rested. A digest MUST NOT substitute for those fields. The presentation MUST show applicable amounts, units, currency, rounding, recipient or account identity, resource or deletion scope, audience and privilege changes without ambiguous labels or silent truncation; localization and accessible alternatives MUST preserve that meaning. The claim MUST declare the consequential fields for each action class and give the approver access to the complete parameters. The presentation MUST be bound to the canonical action released, and a change to its operation, target or consequential parameters MUST invalidate the approval and require a new presentation and approval before release. The evidence MUST record the approver, the presentation's reference and digest, its time, the bound action identity and digest, and the decision; the retained presentation MUST be available to the assessor subject to the retention procedure of ECL1N-0195 to ECL1N-0199.

evidence_obligations: Approval interface, approval records carrying ecl.ext.approval-record.v1, declared minimum review times, approval-rate and review-time monitoring, and decision samples for action classes with a human-approval threshold
requirements.text: For `L2` and above, a claim MUST declare a minimum review time for each action class that requires approval, and an approval recorded sooner than that time after its presentation MUST NOT release the action.

evidence_obligations: Approval interface, approval records carrying ecl.ext.approval-record.v1, declared minimum review times, approval-rate and review-time monitoring, and decision samples for action classes with a human-approval threshold
requirements.text: For `L3` and above, the claimant MUST measure, for each approver and action class, the approval rate and the review times, and MUST treat a declared anomaly, such as more consecutive approvals without a rejection than a declared limit or review times below the declared minimum, as a verification finding that triggers review of that approver's decisions.

evidence_obligations: Approval interface, approval records carrying ecl.ext.approval-record.v1, declared minimum review times, approval-rate and review-time monitoring, and decision samples for action classes with a human-approval threshold
requirements.text: When the Consequential Action Register declares a human-approval threshold for an action class (ECL1N-0007), the Decision Layer MUST NOT return `admit` for an action whose measure is at or above the threshold's value until the approvals of as many distinct authorized persons as the threshold requires are recorded; until then it MUST return `hold` or `challenge`, or `deny` where its verifiable-only outcome or another requirement of this standard requires a `deny`.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: For each in-scope action class, the Consequential Action Register MUST declare, for each decision input that ECL1N-0164 requires it to state, its class as `verifiable`, `actor_supplied`, or `judgment` (Section 4.3), whether the action class requires it, its source, the maximum age of its value, and, when the Decision Layer must obtain it within a set time, its deadline: the time after the Decision Layer receives a request by which it must have the input. An input whose asserted value the governed AI system produces or can overwrite without independent validation, or whose authenticity or transition checks it can modify or bypass, MUST be declared `actor_supplied`; the output of a probabilistic model or heuristic detector about meaning or risk MUST NOT be declared `verifiable`. For each `verifiable` input the claim MUST identify the authority, its validation rules and the controls on freshness, selection and completeness on which an admit relies. An admitted action that causes an independently validated transition MUST NOT by that fact alone make the resulting authoritative observation `actor_supplied`. An actor's selection or omission of authentic observations MUST NOT establish completeness that the authority does not attest or the Decision Layer independently establish. An input that reaches the Decision Layer through the request, or through any channel that the governed AI system can write, MUST be declared `actor_supplied` unless the Decision Layer authenticates its origin as Section 4.3 requires. The Decision Layer MUST NOT consult a decision input that the register does not declare for the action class. The register MUST declare each action class once and each decision input of a class once. For an input that is computed from other declared inputs of the class, the register MUST name those inputs, MUST NOT declare the input `verifiable` unless each of them is `verifiable`, and MUST NOT declare it computed from itself, directly or through other inputs.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: An `actor_supplied` or `judgment` input MUST NOT be the basis of an `admit`. The outcome of a decision MUST be no less strict, in the strictness order of Section 4.3, than its verifiable-only outcome. Such an input MAY make the outcome stricter, including by bringing into effect a detection response declared under ECL1N-0167 and ECL1N-0168, and MUST NOT make it less strict, select an authorization wider than the verifiable-only outcome's, remove an obligation, reduce or defer a consequence-budget debit, or raise or remove a human-approval threshold or lower the number of distinct approvers it requires.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: An `admit` MUST be justified by policy evaluated over `verifiable` inputs alone: its verifiable-only outcome is `admit`, and its authorization is that outcome's authorization or stricter.

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: The evidence of each decision MUST identify, by reference and digest, the version of the Consequential Action Register under which the decision was made, and each decision input that the Decision Layer consulted and each that the register declares for the action class, each input once, with its declared class, whether the action class requires it, whether it was available, late, unavailable, or malformed, its reference and digest when it was available, and its effect on the outcome: `supports` when it is part of the basis on which the verifiable-only outcome permits the action, whatever the final outcome; `restricts` when it made the outcome stricter; and `none` when it had no effect. The decision response MUST carry this record in the registered extension `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1` (DCMP2-053).

evidence_obligations: Consequential Action Register with the class, the required or optional declaration and the derivations of each decision input, write-access configuration of the input sources, policy, decision responses carrying ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, failure-injection records for required and optional inputs, and consequence-budget ledger entries for requests that declare a budget debit
requirements.text: A declared decision input is late when the Decision Layer obtains it after its declared deadline, or when its value is older than its declared maximum age at the time of the decision; it is unavailable when the Decision Layer does not obtain it before it decides, and malformed when it does not have its declared form or its integrity cannot be verified. An input that is unavailable, late, or malformed MUST NOT be part of the basis of an `admit`. If the register declares the input required for the action class, the outcome MUST NOT be `admit`; if the register declares it optional, the input MAY make the outcome stricter and MUST NOT otherwise affect it.

A trusted-time countersignature MUST be an entry of the envelope's `countersignatures` member with `counter_id`, `claim` set to `ecl.claim.trusted-time.v1`, and `attestation`: an ECL-IE-1 envelope, without countersignatures of its own, whose payload type is `application/vnd.ecl.time-attestation+json` and whose payload satisfies `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/time-attestation/1`. Adding one MUST NOT change the covered envelope's payload, payload type, payload digest or signatures, and the producer that adds it MUST increase `envelope_artifact_version` by one (IE1-026). The increment is a producer obligation: a verifier sees one envelope, not its predecessor, and does not check it.

A time attestation MUST bind in `covered` the covered envelope's payload type (`media_type`), its payload digest (`digest`) and the signatures that it attests (`signatures`): for each signature entry of the envelope that it covers, in the envelope's order, the entry's `key_id`, its `suite_id` as `suite`, and as `signature_digest` the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the signature bytes that the entry's `signature` encodes. It MUST carry the attested time in `issued_at` and the time authority in `issuer`, MUST carry an `attestation_id` equal to the entry's `counter_id`, and MUST be signed under its own payload-bound integrity policy, with the verification-time policy `ecl.time.issued-at.v1`, by keys whose trust-policy purpose is `ecl.purpose.trusted-time.v1` and whose principal is the issuer. An attestation attests that the covered payload and the covered signatures existed no later than the attested time; it attests nothing about a signature that it does not cover.

A verifier that evaluates a trusted-time countersignature MUST verify the attestation under the trust-policy version the attestation names, at its attested time, and MUST apply to each of its signing keys the revocations of the caller's current trust policy (TRUST-POLICY-1 TP1-006). A countersignature is invalid, and the covered envelope is not historically valid, with `ecl.error.trusted-time-invalid.v1`, when its claim is not a registered countersignature claim; when the attestation fails that verification, TP1-006, IE1-032 or IE1-033; when an entry of `covered.signatures` names no signature entry of the envelope with that `key_id`, that suite and that signature digest, or the entries are not in the envelope's order or name one signature twice; when its issuer (the attestation's `issuer.id`) is the covered object's own principal, which is `issuer.id` for a DCMP-2 message and `producer.id` for an EBMP-2 record; or when the covered object's own time is later than the attested time. When every trusted-time countersignature of an envelope is valid, the verifier MUST evaluate the historical validity of each signature that a countersignature covers at the earliest attested time among the countersignatures that cover it, and of each other signature at the object's own time, and MUST report the time at which it evaluated each signature. A signature that no countersignature covers, such as one added to the envelope after the attestation, has no attested time; a signature replaced after the attestation makes the countersignature invalid. The threshold of IE1-040 step 7 counts each signature as evaluated at the time this rule gives it. Version 1.0 defines no archive renewal: an attestation carries no countersignature of its own (IE1-032), so a later attestation is one more countersignature, verified on its own, and does not protect an earlier one.

A verification profile MAY require trusted time. Under such a profile a verifier MUST refuse an envelope that carries no trusted-time countersignature, or one of whose signature entries no trusted-time countersignature covers, as not historically valid, with `ecl.error.trusted-time-required.v1`. The gateway MUST NOT run in a process, container or account that the governed AI system can start, stop or configure, or in which it can execute code.

The gateway MUST treat as side-effecting, and send to the Decision Layer before forwarding, every `tools/call` request (including a retry that carries `inputResponses` or `requestState`), every `tasks/update` request for a task that a governed tool call created, and every other request that the Consequential Action Register maps to a consequential action class, such as a `resources/read` that discloses non-public data. It MUST refuse, with code -31007, every request whose method the claim neither maps to an action class nor lists as forwarded without a decision, and every `tools/call` for a tool that has no mapping. The claim MAY list `server/discover`, the list requests of the pinned revision (`tools/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list` and `prompts/list`) and `subscriptions/listen` as forwarded without a decision, unless the register classifies them as consequential, and MUST NOT list any other request. The claim MAY list for forwarding without a decision only notifications that the pinned revision defines for a client, and MUST NOT list one that the register maps to a consequential action class; the gateway MUST NOT forward any other notification from the governed AI system. As JSON-RPC 2.0 requires, it returns no response to a notification.

Each in-scope tool MUST have a mapping declared with the Consequential Action Register that names the server (identifier, name and version), the tool name, the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the tool definition as reviewed, the action class, the operation, the rule that derives the target from the call's arguments, and the evidence profile; the gateway MUST take the action class, operation and target of the decision request from that mapping, and never from the governed AI system's request or from the tool's own annotations.

The decision request MUST carry the call's `arguments` object, read from its RFC 8785 canonical form, as `action.parameters`, with `action.parameters_digest` its digest under DCMP2-007, and MUST carry the registered extension `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1`, marked critical, naming the server, the tool, the tool-definition digest and the mapping, and the digests of any `inputResponses` and `requestState` that the call carries; the gateway MUST refuse, and not forward, a call whose arguments, read from their RFC 8785 canonical form, are outside the restricted canonical JSON profile (IE1-001). A decision point that evaluates such a request MUST check that the mapping and the tool-definition digest it names are the reviewed ones that its register holds for that server and tool, and MUST NOT admit the request otherwise. The decision request MUST also carry, in `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1`, `params_digest`: the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the call's complete `params` object, `_meta` included. The gateway MUST refuse with -31007, and not forward, a request that has a member other than `jsonrpc`, `id`, `method` and `params`, or whose `id` or `params` holds a number that RFC 8785 does not represent exactly: a number of magnitude greater than 2^53 - 1, beyond the range [-(2^53)+1, (2^53)-1] that RFC 7493 section 2.2 gives for exact integers, or any other number whose RFC 8785 form does not have the value written.

requirements.text: The gateway MUST forward a side-effecting request only after it has verified a DCMP-2 `admit` for exactly that request under DCMP2-HTTP-1 and the claim's trust policy, only within its use policy, only after it has discharged every pre-release obligation of the admit (MG1-013), and only through the release order of MG1-014, at a final observation of its clock that is no earlier than the authorization's `valid_from` and that, with the release guard added, is earlier than its `valid_until`; it MUST forward exactly the call that the admitted request binds: the forwarded request's `method` and `params` MUST be the call's, `params` MUST have the digest `params_digest`, and the gateway MUST NOT add, remove or change any member of the call. The gateway counts the uses of an authorization in the instance that holds them, so a deployment MUST route every use of an authorization through one gateway instance, or share the use store among its instances by a mechanism that this profile does not specify, so that the count of ECL1N-0186 item 3 covers every instance.

For every request that it does not forward, the gateway MUST return a JSON-RPC error response with the code that the error table of this profile gives for the cause and a `data.ecl` member naming the cause and its registered reason, and MUST NOT return a `result`; the codes lie outside the range that JSON-RPC 2.0 reserves (-32768 to -32000), as the pinned MCP text asks of application-defined errors. When more than one cause holds, the gateway MUST return the code of the first that holds in this order: -31007, -31008, -31004, -31005, then the code of the decision's outcome (-31001, -31002 or -31003), then -31010, -31011 and -31006. A pre-release obligation that the gateway has not discharged when it refuses is unproven, so the refusal of an admit that carries one is -31010, whether or not its authorization is also unusable. A record cannot show that the gateway's journal failed (-31011, MG1-017), so a checker that reads a record whose refusal is -31011 checks only that no earlier cause holds.

When the decision service cannot be reached, does not answer within the declared total timeout, or answers with anything other than a verified decision response for the request, the gateway MUST NOT forward the request, MUST return the error for an unavailable or invalid decision, and MUST NOT retry within the decision attempt (DHB1-007, DHB1-008). A decision response that does not carry exactly one `ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1`, or whose decision basis fails DCMP2-053 with the record's `decision_request` as the request it answers, with the response clock-skew allowance of the reference verification profile, zero (DCMP2-047), is not a verified decision response, and a record that holds such a response as an answered decision MUST be reported with `ecl.rule.decision-basis-one-way.v1`. Each DCMP-2 message that the record holds, other than the `response` of a `decision` whose `status` is `invalid`, MUST satisfy the semantic rules of DCMP-2, and a record that holds one that fails a rule MUST be reported with that rule.

A tool added to or removed from an in-scope server's tool list, a change to any member of a tool definition, and a change of the server's name or version in `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo` MUST be treated as a control change that requires review under ECL1N-0170: the gateway MUST compare the current definition, obtained from `tools/list`, with the mapped digest before it forwards a call, and MUST refuse calls to a changed or added tool, and to every tool of a server whose identity or version changed, until the change is reviewed and the mapping updated.

evidence_obligations: An inventory of the credentials, tokens, keys and connections that reach in-scope servers, with their holders; the gateway's trust anchors, redirect setting and message limits
requirements.text: The governed AI system MUST NOT hold a credential, token, key or connection that reaches an in-scope server or a system that one of its tools reaches; the gateway, or a credential broker behind it, MUST hold that material, MUST use it only for forwarded requests, and MUST NOT pass a credential that the governed AI system presents to the gateway on to a server.

The gateway MUST record EBMP-2 evidence for each side-effecting request as an enforcement point: for a forwarded request, `authority_consumed`, `release_prepared`, `execution_released`, which carries the discharge of MG1-013 when the admit carries a pre-release obligation, and an `execution_terminal` event that carries `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1` with the `ecl.digest.sha-256.v1` digest of the RFC 8785 canonical form of the response the server returned and the forward's completion (MG1-015); for a refused request, an `execution_terminal` event in the non-release state that EBMP2-051 gives, or in state `cancelled` when the gateway consumed the authorization before it refused (MG1-014). The response the gateway returns to the governed AI system for a forwarded request MUST be the response whose digest the evidence records, with one exception: the gateway MUST NOT return a server error that uses a code of the error table, and returns such an error with its `error.code` replaced by -32603 and every other member unchanged.

evidence_obligations: An inventory of the credentials, tokens, keys and connections that reach in-scope servers, with their holders; the gateway's trust anchors, redirect setting and message limits
requirements.text: The gateway MUST authenticate the decision service and each in-scope server with TLS under trust anchors that its operator configures, with plain HTTP only on the loopback interface and only when explicitly enabled for testing; it MUST NOT follow redirects from either, and MUST apply the DCMP2-HTTP-1 limits to decision exchanges and declared limits to MCP messages before parsing them.

A gateway that retains exchange records MUST write each one as `ecl_mcp_gateway_exchange_v1`, valid against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/binding/mcp-gateway-exchange/1`, and every value of `ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1` it emits MUST validate against `https://externalcontrollayer.ai/ns/schema/extension/mcp-binding/1`. A record member that holds MCP content (`call`, `tool_definition`, the `request` of `forwarded`, `server_response` and `returned`) MUST hold it as the JSON object itself when the content, read from its RFC 8785 canonical form, lies within the restricted canonical JSON profile (IE1-001), and otherwise as an object whose only member, `rfc8785`, is the canonical base64, with padding, of the content's RFC 8785 canonical bytes. A checker MUST treat a record as failing its schema when such a member does not decode to the RFC 8785 canonical form of a JSON object that lies outside the restricted profile, or when the content it decodes does not satisfy the definition that the record schema gives the same content held as itself (`jsonRpcRequest` for the call and the forwarded request, `jsonRpcResponse` for the server's response and the response returned, and `toolDefinition` for the tool definition), and otherwise MUST apply this profile's rules to the content it decodes.
